newsitem.title: USA: Clinton mulls legal options on affirmative action.
newsitem.headline: Clinton mulls legal options on affirmative action.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he was exploring "what our legal options are" to preserve preferential admission policies for minority students at federally-funded colleges and universities.

Clinton's statement, in a question-and answer session with a group of Hispanic-Americans, came on the same day the U.S. Supreme Court dealt the administration a setback by agreeing to review a potentially far-reaching affirmative action case.

"I'm not willing to give up on affirmative action in education. I'm not about to give up on it, and we are exploring what our legal options are as well as what policies we might implement to try to stop public high education in America from becoming resegregated," Clinton said.
He did not elaborate, but the study of options is presumably part of a year-long presidential initiative that will examine U.S. racial problems and ways to solve them.

Clinton, who spoke via satellite to a convention of the League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) in Anaheim, Calif., made no mention of the high court's decision to review a lower court ruling on a New Jersey school district action.
The ruling held that school districts may not take racial diversity into account when laying off a white teacher over an equally qualified black teacher.

Justice Department lawyers expressed concern that the high court's decision to intervene might lead to further restrictions, if not a complete ban, on certain affirmative action programmes for blacks and other minorities.
Clinton opposed California Proposition 209, a referendum approved by the state's voters last year which ordered the repeal of affirmative action programmes in education and hiring.

In a San Diego speech on June 14, Clinton said Prop. 209 had already dramatically affected minority enrollment in the state's university system even though legal challenges have so far blocked its implemention.
